zones.what: Lifeboats are mounted at Deck 7; they obstruct downward and partial lateral views from Decks 8, 9, and 10, with Deck 8 experiencing the most severe obstruction and Deck 10 the least.
zones.effect: Balconies look down at orange boat covers instead of water; horizon views remain clear, and the boats provide some wind shelter.
zones.mattersTo: Matters greatly to guests who want unobstructed water views directly below; irrelevant to those focused on horizon, sunset, or port views, or to inside/oceanview cabins.

zones.what: The main pool deck, outdoor buffet seating, and pools are directly above on Deck 16 midship and aft.
zones.effect: Daytime foot traffic, deck chair scraping, and pool activity create noise overhead from early morning through evening; heaviest midday.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to light sleepers, those napping during the day, or anyone sensitive to overhead noise; less relevant to guests out and about during peak pool hours.

zones.what: The Waterfront outdoor dining and walking promenade on Deck 8 is six decks below.
zones.effect: This deck-to-deck relationship does not materially change cabin experience.
zones.mattersTo: Not applicable — no material impact on cabin experience.

zones.what: The Escape Theater (main showroom) sits on Decks 6 and 7 directly below the forward sections.
zones.effect: Show nights bring bass, music, and applause until 10-11 PM; the theater is dark some nights, making this intermittent.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to early sleepers and families with young children on show nights; irrelevant to night owls or those out at evening entertainment.

zones.what: The Haven sundeck, pool, and hot tubs are directly below on Deck 17 forward (which also has cabins).
zones.effect: Daytime and evening Haven guest activity creates foot traffic and conversation noise below, though Haven areas tend to be quieter than main pools.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to Haven guests on Deck 16 who are light sleepers or value midday quiet; the activity level is much lower than the main pool deck.

zones.what: The Haven sundeck, pool, and hot tubs on Deck 17 have the observation deck and walking area directly above on Deck 18.
zones.effect: Foot traffic and conversation from the observation deck create minor noise overhead, typically during the day and at sunset.
zones.mattersTo: Matters minimally; the observation deck is not a high-activity venue and Haven guests expect some shared-space proximity.

zones.what: Primary elevator banks run midship through all main guest decks with lobbies and machine rooms creating structural noise and guest traffic.
zones.effect: Cabins adjacent to elevator shafts hear chimes, door mechanisms, and hydraulic hums 24/7; cabins near lobbies get hallway conversation and foot traffic at embark/debark and port days.
zones.mattersTo: Matters significantly to light sleepers and those sensitive to mechanical hum; convenient for guests prioritizing fast vertical access over quiet.

zones.what: Deck 5 sits low in the hull where propulsion vibration and engine hum are most perceptible, particularly in the forward and midship machinery spaces.
zones.effect: Low-frequency vibration and a faint but constant hum are present underway; most noticeable at night in quiet cabins and when the ship is at cruising speed.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to vibration-sensitive guests and light sleepers; less relevant to sound sleepers, those who run white noise, or guests who are rarely in the cabin.

zones.what: Bow thruster machinery sits low and forward; anchor chain runs through the bow on Deck 5 forward and is audible on Decks 8 and 9 forward during anchoring.
zones.effect: Every port morning where the ship anchors (not docks), the anchor chain creates loud metallic rumbling for 1-3 minutes, typically between 6-8 AM.
zones.mattersTo: Matters greatly to late sleepers on tender port days; irrelevant on docked days or to early risers already awake.

zones.what: The superstructure extends outboard past the lifeboat line midship on these decks, giving balconies a cantilever that juts beyond the hull.
zones.effect: These balconies sit lower and more central (smoother ride), clear the lifeboats entirely for unobstructed water views, and typically price lower than higher decks despite the better view geometry.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to value-focused cruisers wanting balcony views without lifeboat obstruction and those who prefer midship stability; less relevant to guests prioritizing high-deck status or aft location.

zones.what: Crew access points to the I-95 crew corridor sit forward and aft on guest cabin decks, with service doors, crew foot traffic, and cart movement during early morning and late night service hours.
zones.effect: Service activity creates door noise, cart rolling, and crew conversation from roughly 5-7 AM (breakfast prep) and 9 PM-midnight (turndown, galley service); intermittent but predictable.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to light sleepers in cabins near crew access doors, especially those who sleep during service hours; irrelevant to guests out of the cabin during these times.

zones.what: The Studio complex (solo cabins with shared lounge) occupies a dedicated section midship on Deck 11 with 16 interior-access cabins.
zones.effect: Studios share a private keycard-access lounge and have inward-facing doors to an interior corridor, creating a distinct micro-community separate from the main hallway traffic.
zones.mattersTo: Matters only to solo travelers booking Studios; the separate entry and lounge make it a different cabin experience than standard inside cabins.

zones.what: The Spa cabins on Decks 11 and 12 forward include access to the Mandara Spa thermal suite and priority spa booking.
zones.effect: These cabins are marketed with spa access as the differentiator; the location is forward and low, subject to the same bow motion and anchor noise as non-spa cabins in this section.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to guests prioritizing spa amenities and willing to accept forward/low location trade-offs; the spa perks, not location, are the value.

zones.what: The Haven is a ship-within-a-ship complex on Decks 17 and 18 forward with private keycard access, dedicated pool, sundeck, restaurant, and concierge.
zones.effect: Haven guests experience restricted access (secure elevator and stairwell), exclusive amenities, and separation from the main guest flow; cabins here are suites with butler service.
zones.mattersTo: Matters only to guests booking Haven suites; this is a premium enclave with different service, pricing, and access than the rest of the ship.

unknowns: Exact placement of galley exhaust vents and whether they affect specific aft or midship sections on any deck.
